key_insight: PoreML is an open-source, physics-grounded framework that unifies data generation, model training, and evaluation to advance machine learning for multiphase flow in porous media.
engineering_relevance: It can help engineers build more reliable predictive tools for applications such as CO2 storage, fuel-cell operation, and porous microstructure design where fluid-interface dynamics are hard to simulate and optimize.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale data generation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries
Unified benchmark for one-step prediction, autoregressive rollout, and physical-consistency evaluation
evidence_signal: The framework evaluates five model architectures using domain-specific protocols and includes two transfer challenges: scaling to larger domains and generalizing from synthetic to micro-CT-derived structures.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on data coverage and geometry transfer, so models validated on PoreML may still struggle when wettability, pore structure, or domain size shift outside the benchmark distribution.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
